content.title: Why Audiences Are So Excited About A24's 'Backrooms'
content.text: Published Apr 1, 2026, 4:00 PM EDT Bill Dubiel is a veteran writer, editor, and college professor based in Buffalo, NY. Formerly of Screen Rant, you can usually find him in a late-night double feature, including the newest horror movie, a neo-Western, or the latest Godzilla adventure. A24 has an incredible track record in producing some of the most acclaimed horror hits of the last decade, including iconic movies like Hereditary, Midsommar, and the X trilogy. Their latest offering is Backrooms, a supernatural sci-fi horror experience that has skyrocketed up horror fans’ priority list since its unsettling trailer was released. Starring Chiwetel Ejiofor and Renate Reinsve, Backrooms is set to release domestically on May 29th, 2026, from director Kane Parsons in his feature film debut. In addition to Backrooms’ endorsement from A24, the movie is backed by a litany of big-name producers/directors, including horror legend James Wan, Shawn Levy (Stranger Things, Deadpool & Wolverine), Dan Levine (Arrival), and Osgood Perkins (Longlegs). With so much star power behind it, along with a relatively sizable budget, Backrooms has all the pieces in place for an instant horror classic. But what sets it apart from other similarly-hyped horror movies is the online community that has been driving excitement through the roof ever since the project was first announced in February 2023. 'Backrooms' Is Based on a Viral 4CHAN Thread The concept of The Backrooms originated in 2019 as a creepypasta on 4chan, and has been characterized as a seemingly endless maze of empty rooms that exist outside our reality. The Backrooms are a prime example of “liminal space”, or seemingly abandoned spaces that appear eerie due to their emptiness. While the concept originated with a single photo of a retail store under renovation, the internet community has expanded the idea to include different levels, hostile entities, and additional lore. The Backrooms’ aesthetic is particularly distinct, and includes pale yellow walls with simplistic wallpaper, the absence of furniture or decoration in most rooms, and the never-ending buzz of fluorescent lighting. What is recognized as the original description from an anonymous user on 4chan reads: If you’re not careful and you noclip out of reality in the wrong areas, you’ll end up in the Backrooms, where it’s nothing but the stink of old moist carper, the madness of mono-yellow, the endless background noise of fluorescent lights at maximum hum-buzz, and approximately six hundred million square miles of randomly segmented empty rooms to be trapped in God save you if you hear something wandering around nearby, because it sure as hell heard you. The Backrooms can be accessed by "noclipping"—a video game term referring to a cheat code ability to walk through walls and other objects—out of reality, and the trailer reveals a couple of instances of its characters doing just that. 'Backrooms' 20-Year-Old Director Is the YouTuber Who Created the Original 'The Backrooms' Web Series A24 Several studios have rolled the dice on first-time filmmakers in horror lately, and they’ve been rewarded with excellent movies. A24 is doing the same with Backrooms, which will be directed by Kane Parsons, the 20-year-old YouTube creator known as “Kane Pixels” to the online community. While the concept of The Backrooms started on 4chan, it was Parsons’ viral 23-episode web series delving into the lore and background of the extradimensional space that truly elevated it to new heights. Parsons’ acclaimed work on the web series, which originated in 2022 when he was still a teenager, is directly responsible for his involvement with the A24 feature film. Parsons' web series was crafted as a found-footage series, as reflected in the trailer, exploring the location and the government entities involved, along with some of the entities that lurked within. Parsons' own visual interpretation of the concept, which he created as a self-taught animator in Blender, heavily informs the movie's visuals. While studios and producers undoubtedly had input, it's important to note that, based on the trailer, Backrooms will be almost entirely Kane Parsons' vision. 'Backrooms' Has Award-Winning Producers and Two Academy Award Nominees as Its Leads A24 A24's endorsement is impactful on its own, but the litany of award-winning producers attached to the movie takes Backrooms to another level. The list of accomplished producers includes horror legend James Wan (Saw, The Conjuring), Shawn Levy (Stranger Things, Deadpool & Wolverine), Osgood Perkins (Longlegs), and Dan Levine (Arrival), among other notable names. While the vision might be Parsons', it's clear that he has experience and talent in his corner, weighing in and supporting his feature film debut, which is likely a big reason why A24 felt comfortable giving a directing rookie like Parsons the opportunity to make things his way. As if all those names weren't enough, Parsons was also fortunate enough to be working with two exceptionally talented Academy Award-nominated artists in front of the camera. Backrooms stars Chiwetel Ejiofor (12 Years a Slave) as the main character, Clark; the accomplished British actor has an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor to his name in addition to multiple Primetime Emmy nominations that highlight a list of accolades too long to list. Opposite Ejiofor is Renate Reinsve, the Norwegian actress fresh off her own Academy Award nomination for Best Actress for her work in 2025's Sentimental Value. The cast also includes horror genre icon Mark Duplass (Creep), Finn Bennett (A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms), Lukita Maxwell (Shrinking), and Avan Jogia (Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City). The human cast is understandably limited given the concept, but there are bound to be some additional non-human entities lurking in the shadows of Backrooms.
